newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to cut tax deductions to boost consumption.
newsitem.headline: Spain to cut tax deductions to boost consumption.

text.p: Spain said on Monday it will soon approve a 2.7-percent cut in its tax deductions on income at source to adjust for inflation in taxes on wages and salaries and to boost lacklustre consumer spending.
The government plans to approve a new table with modified tax brackets for tax deductions, but it will leave the tax tariffs themselves unchanged.
The change will reduce overall tax receipts by around 80 billion pesetas, but it will also reduce tax refunds.
"The government will approve it (this project) by the end of the month. It could be as soon as this Friday's meeting," a spokeswoman for the Secretary of the Exchequer said on Monday.
She added the measure is expected to boost private consumption.
Industry sources said the number of tax brackets will be reduced to 26 from the former 27, and tax deductions at source on income will be cut by 2.7 percent.
The minimum taxable income will be raised by 13 percent to 1.21 million pesetas from 1.07 million.
